title: How does the hub talk to its agents?
context: The hub is a separate small app (decision 6). Agents work as usual, post a summary when they finish a round, then wait for a reply from the orchestrator or from you. The hub has to send replies into agents that are idle and waiting.

options.name: Hub hosts its agents
options.summary: The hub starts every agent, orchestrators included, through the Claude Agent SDK, so it can send to them and read their output whenever it likes.

pros: Full control: send, stream, interrupt, read status
No preview features, no hook timing
You already know this pattern well
cons: Sessions started elsewhere (a terminal) are outside it
The hub must handle permission prompts itself

options.name: Agents join through a channel
options.summary: Agents run wherever you start them, launched with a Crux channel server that carries messages both ways.

cons: Every agent must be started with the flag

options.name: Hosted, with a channel later
options.summary: Start with hub-hosted agents; add the channel later so terminal sessions can join the same board.

recommendation: Hosting agents in the hub is stable and squarely in your wheelhouse; the message format should not care how an agent connects, so a channel can be added when you want terminal sessions on the board.
